newsitem.title: GREECE: Xiosbank says H1 earnings grew 110 pct.
newsitem.headline: Xiosbank says H1 earnings grew 110 pct.

text.p: Xiosbank said its first-half pretax earnings jumped 110 percent to 2.1 billion drachmas from 1.0 billion in the same period a year earlier.
Xiosbank expects to beat its earlier 1997 earnings forecast of 2.7 billion drachmas. The bank earned 2.1 billion in 1996.
The profit rise was attributed to a strong increase in its loan portfolio which was financed by a growing deposit base, it said.
As of end-June, corporate loans made up 43 percent of Xiosbank's loan portfolio with consumer credit accounting for 57 percent.
Total loans in the first-half reached 127.3 billion drachmas, up 41.1 percent versus 90.1 billion in the first-half a year earlier. They stood at 102.5 at the end of 1996.
Deposits grew 51.8 percent year-on-year to 174.6 billion drachmas. They amounted to 183.4 billion at the end of 1996. Total assets also rose 57.3 percent to 420.6 billion, it said.
Xiosbank's fund management arm had 139.1 billion drachmas in assets under management at the end of the first half, a growth of 135 percent year-on-year.
